sn56.19:1.2: A parallel phrase dealing with the skillful and unskillful is found at [an4.188:3.2](), except it says “words, phrasings, and teachings of the Realized One”. Taken together with the next line, these passages are saying that these basic teachings are expressed in countless different ways. | Take _vaṇṇā_ here in the sense “order, arrangement, presentation”, otherwise attested only for Sanskrit _varṇa_. | _Saṅkāsanā_, from root _kās_ (“shine”) is unique in early Pali, but in late canonical Pali it appears with several other terms in an expansion of the current passage, evidently having the sense “illustration” ([ne4:32.2](), [pe1:32.1]()).
sn56.19:1.3: Literally, “Thus also, ‘This is the noble truth of suffering’.”
